leads.text: The exported Express XSS-sanitization middleware (module.exports.xss = middleware, in index.js) explicitly sanitizes req.body, req.params, req.headers, and req.query via sanitize(req[k], options), but never includes 'cookies' in the sanitized-keys list and never touches req.cookies. In a typical Express stack where cookie-parser runs before this middleware, req.cookies is a standard attacker-controlled input source (per the briefing's own source list) that completely bypasses this library's only protective control, so any value read from req.cookies.* still reaches downstream rendering/sinks unsanitized even though the app believes 'xss' middleware is scrubbing all request input.
leads.evidence: run_cypher on CpgCall/CpgMethod for file_path='index.js' returned the full middleware body: "function middleware(options = {}) { return (req, res, next) => { ['body', 'params', 'headers'].forEach((k) => { if (req[k]) { req[k] = sanitize(req[k], options); } }); const sanitizedQuery = sanitize(req.query, options); Object.defineProperty(req, 'query', {...}); next(); }; }" -- the literal array ['body','params','headers'] plus a separate req.query assignment are the only sanitized surfaces; 'cookies' does not appear anywhere in index.js or lib/sanitize.js (confirmed via full CpgCall sweep of both files, 2 files total in CpgFile for this scan, and semantic_search returning the identical full-file text for index.js).

leads.text: sanitize-html (~2.13.0) is the sole third-party sanitization engine this package delegates all XSS neutralization to (lib/sanitize.js calls sanitizeHtml(data, options.sanitizerOptions) for every string field of req.body/req.params/req.headers/req.query). The call graph confirms this is the highest-centrality reachable method in the whole package (centrality 0.01177, reachable_from_entry=true, hop_distance=0), i.e. a single chokepoint: any sanitize-html parsing/filter bypass in the declared 2.13.0 line defeats this entire middleware's protection for every consumer. The declared range is a tight tilde (~2.13.0, patch-only), so it will not auto-pick-up a newer minor release that fixes a parser/filter-bypass advisory discovered after 2.13.0 shipped. Recommend the verifier diff 2.13.0 against the current sanitize-html changelog/advisory list for any filter-bypass or ReDoS fix landed after that version.
leads.evidence: MATCH (d:Dependency {scan_id:$scan_id}) RETURN d.name, d.version -> sanitize-html ~2.13.0. Cross-checked with MATCH (m:CpgMethod {scan_id:$scan_id}) RETURN m.full_name,... -> lib/sanitize.js::program:sanitize has centrality=0.011770019107173875, reachable_from_entry=true, hop_distance=0 (highest centrality of any method in the scan), and semantic_search('regular expression pattern validation catastrophic backtracking') surfaced lib/sanitize.js's sanitize() as the function that pipes every req.body/params/headers/query string field through sanitizeHtml(). exploit_search was attempted for 'sanitize-html vulnerability bypass' but the corpus is unindexed in this environment, so this is unverified against a CVE list -- flagging the version/chokepoint combination for the independent verifier to check against sanitize-html's advisory history.

leads.text: Declared dependency body-parser is pinned with a floating caret range (^1.19.0 = >=1.19.0 <2.0.0), which does not exclude pre-1.20.3 releases. body-parser has a publicly documented DoS weakness in versions prior to 1.20.3 (urlencoded parsing). Because the range is unbounded below 2.0.0 and not floor-pinned above the fixed patch, a fresh install without an existing lockfile pin could resolve to a vulnerable 1.x version. This is a components-with-known-vulnerabilities concern independent of any specific request flow.
leads.evidence: MATCH (d:Dependency {scan_id:$scan_id}) RETURN d.name, d.version ORDER BY name -> returned body-parser ^1.19.0 among the 12 declared Dependency nodes for this scan_id. exploit_search('body-parser denial of service vulnerability') returned no results (corpus unindexed in this environment) so the specific advisory could not be independently confirmed this session -- flagging the unpinned version range itself as the candidate issue for the verifier to check against the resolved lockfile version and body-parser's security advisories.

leads.text: express is declared at ^5.0.1, i.e. the first patch release of the newly-GA'd Express 5 major line, with a caret range open to any later 5.x. Express is not actually `require()`'d anywhere in this package's own two source files (index.js, lib/sanitize.js) -- it only appears as a declared Dependency node, implying it (and body-parser/supertest/mocha/chai) are consumed by this package's own test harness rather than shipped runtime logic. Still worth a version/advisory sanity check since it is a floating range on a very recent major version with limited field-hardening history relative to the long-lived 4.x line.
leads.evidence: MATCH (d:Dependency {scan_id:$scan_id}) RETURN d.name, d.version -> express ^5.0.1. Cross-checked against the full CpgCall dump (148 rows, index.js + lib/sanitize.js) which contains only require('./lib/sanitize') and require('sanitize-html') -- no require('express') or require('body-parser') call exists in the indexed source, so express's actual usage site is outside the two files captured by this scan (most likely the test suite). exploit_search('express 5 vulnerability open redirect') returned no results (corpus unindexed).
